title: Coastal shipping cabotage regime (Coastal Trading Act)
summary: The Coastal Trading (Revitalising Australian Shipping) Act 2012 replaced the permit system with general (Australian-registered vessels), temporary and emergency licences for coastal trading, restricting foreign vessels to voyage-limited temporary licences.
direction_rationale: Licensing preferences for Australian-flagged ships and conditions on temporary licences raise barriers for foreign vessels in coastal freight, which the PC and Harper review saw as reducing competition.
comparison: none: national change; possible contrast by state reliance on coastal shipping (e.g. Tasmania, WA) or by freight-intensive industries (cement, sugar, fuel)
notes: Business counts in Water Freight Transport are small; better suited to industry-specific freight-rate studies.

assessment.summary: Licences for coastal shipping favour Australian-registered vessels and restrict foreign ships to voyage-limited temporary licences. The Harper Review and the Productivity Commission found it raises freight costs and reduces competition.

marks.reason: Restricts foreign vessels to voyage-limited temporary licences, closing much of coastal freight to the cheapest ships.
Temporary licence applications, notices and variations add delay and cost for shippers.
